top_level_observations.observation: Most facets are IDENTIFIED correctly. The errors are in LINE PLACEMENT, and they are NOT systematic.
top_level_observations.from_: overview pass, before the per-facet pass
top_level_observations.why_it_matters: non-systematic placement error points at the segmentation boundary rather than at a global parameter, and it rules out a whole class of fixes before anyone proposes one: no single threshold, offset or erosion width can correct an error that is not consistent.

identity.correct: this facet corresponds to one real roof plane
identity.merge: this facet and another are ONE real plane split in two
identity.split: this facet is TWO real planes fitted as one
identity.spurious: no real roof plane here at all

boundary.tight: outline follows the real roof edge
boundary.short: outline stops INSIDE the real roof edge; roof continues past it
boundary.over: outline extends PAST the real edge onto something that is not this facet
boundary.ragged: roughly right but jagged where the real edge is straight
boundary.cut: outline CROSSES a real roof feature (ridge, valley, dormer) instead of stopping at it

instructions.note: free text. Say what you SAW, not what the fix should be. A physical description travels to the next site; a suggested threshold does not.

facets.note: SW corner is a super thick solid pink blob. the main problem is that the pink line exetnds way past the facet going south and slightly north (onto facets 1, 7, 4, and 5). In ohter word, mask contains thin disconnected fragments remote from it: stray contour lines running off across the building enclosing nothing, confirmed as facet 0's (they turn cyan when another facet is selected). Reads as plane-vs-facet: assignment is by distance to an unbounded plane, so points far away that happen to lie within inlier distance join the facet. Single-ownership and disconnection guards do not catch thin remote slivers. Need boundary code "fragmented" (mask includes disconnected pieces remote from the main body), distinct from "over". Open question, do not act yet: does facet_area compute over the whole mask or the largest connected component only? If the whole mask, this inflates the deliverable.

capture_note.what_happened: The 'add a missing facet' and 'add a missing line' buttons in review.html did nothing. Cause: el() built elements inside a <div>, and the HTML parser DISCARDS <tr>/<td> outside table context, so el('<tr>...') returned null, appendChild(null) threw, and render() aborted. No message reached the reviewer; the lists simply stayed empty.
capture_note.consequence: missing_facets and missing_lines did NOT come through the same path as the per-facet verdicts. They were dictated afterwards and are marked source='dictated, UI capture failed' so a reader can weigh them accordingly.
capture_note.fixed: scripts/review_ui.py now builds elements through <template>, which parses table rows correctly, and el() throws instead of returning null. Both add buttons now verify that the on-screen row count matches the state array and alert the reviewer if it does not.
capture_note.classification: Same family as the four failures in decisions/2026-07-27-silent-failure-standing-rule.md: well-formed, plausible, silent, wrong.

schema_note_for_pass_2.problem: The identity code `merge` is defined as 'this facet and another are ONE real plane split in two' (over-segmentation). Some rows used it in the OPPOSITE sense: 'this facet has taken in area that is not part of it' (absorption). Those are different mechanisms, M3 and M1b respectively, and one code cannot carry both.

change_for_pass_2.absorbed: NEW CODE: this facet has taken in area that is not part of it (foreign structure, chimney, dormer edge, neighbouring facet; mechanism M1b)
